correctness.rationale: The base first integral has positive diagonal Hessian, a unique positive minimum and compact sublevel sets in the positive quadrant. Every regular level is the boundary of a strictly convex planar sublevel, hence a smooth oval; the nonvanishing tangent field makes it a periodic orbit. With P=VW, (log P)'=G, so the pairwise model preserves U/P and the higher-order addition cancels at U=(b/d)P. Uniqueness gives equality from the same on-graph start. Off the graph S=bP/(dU)−1 solves S'=−bPS in the higher-order model and S'=0 in the pairwise model. The explicit solution retains S>−1 forward, so U=bP/[d(1+S)] stays positive and exists globally. Period averages of (log W)' and V' give mean VW=αδ/(κγ). This verifies the exact higher-order Floquet exponent and the multiplier over each period; the instantaneous rate is −bVW and need not be constant. The pairwise multiplier is 1; no orbital attraction of individual cycles is claimed. The shift in the common state's per-capita U derivative under a positive-octant U perturbation ε is −dε, giving immediate separation. The bound supporting program was inspected, not executed; the checks reported by the record do not certify the all-time statements.

value.rationale: The construction separates complete observational equivalence from dynamical response without changing measured coordinates, invoking noise or shortening the observation window. The exact normal multiplier explains why the higher-order system returns to the indistinguishable surface while the pairwise system does not, and the one-coordinate perturbation gives a concrete way to discriminate the two models. The conclusion is a useful structural counterexample, not evidence of generic ecological prevalence.
